app_settings.auto_check_help: Allomos asks GitHub once a day whether a newer version exists. When this is off, it asks only when you choose Check for Updates… in the menu.
app_settings.auto_download_help: After a check finds a newer version, Allomos downloads and checks its installer in the background. When this is off, nothing is downloaded in the background; Check for Updates… still downloads.

agentline.unshared_hint: Allomos saves your changes but never runs your version control tool. The next AI agent that changes a task is shown them, with the files to save and share as yours (for Git, the commands).
agentline.label: AI agents:
agentline.popup_title: Quota left, as the agents reported it
agentline.popup_none: No agent has reported its quota on this computer yet. Agents report it with alm quota when they check their quota for the handoff.

agents.how_paste: will open a terminal; the request will be on the clipboard to paste

agents.claude_app_trust: The Claude app may first ask you to trust this folder: choose Trust workspace, or the session starts without the project.
agents.none: No AI agent was found on this computer. Choose Manual to paste the request into any AI agent, or let Allomos add its instructions to AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md itself.

manual.waiting: After you send it, Allomos notices here when the agent has written AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. Choose Done when you have sent it.
manual.seen: ✓ The agent has added Allomos's instructions to {files}. Choose Done.
manual.pending: Send the copied request in your AI agent. Allomos tells you when the agent has added its instructions.
manual.finished: Your AI agent added Allomos's instructions to {files}.
confirm.from_unknown: An AI agent asks before changing this project:
confirm.scope: Go ahead covers only what is shown here. If the plan changes afterwards, the agent asks you again.
confirm.cancelled: Cancelled: nothing was changed. To ask again, tell the AI agent in its window, for example "I changed my mind — please show me the plan again", or choose File → Connect with the Agents… to start again with any agent.
progress.from_unknown: An AI agent is working on this job:
progress.finished_unknown: The AI agent finished this job and says:
progress.waiting: Waiting for the AI agent to respond… Send the request in the agent's window if you have not yet.
progress.quiet: The agent has not reported for 10 minutes. It may be waiting for your reply in its window, or it may have stopped. If you close this, it comes back when the agent reports again.

settings.scope_taskbag: Changes here affect only this taskbag, and are shared with everyone who uses it.

settings.task_language_note: AI agents write new and changed tasks in this language. Existing tasks are not translated; Translate the Taskbag… below rewrites them.
folders.note: Add every folder this project's work happens in, such as a code, a website and a mobile repository. They share these tasks, and each folder's AGENTS.md points its AI agents back to this taskbag.
folders.bind_title: Choose a folder to bind to this taskbag
folders.unbind_tasks: {count} task(s) name this folder ({open} still open). They stay; the folder's name is taken off them.
folders.unbind_files: The folder's files stay where they are.
folders.unbind_section: Only the Allomos section leaves its AGENTS.md.

pane.difficulty_title: How hard the task is, from 1 (very easy) to 5 (very hard), as the agent that added it judged. A task without one counts as 3.
problem.difficulty_invalid: {value} is not a difficulty: use a whole number from 1 (very easy) to 5 (very hard).
problem.difficulty_range_invalid: {value} is not a difficulty range: use two levels from 1 to 5 with a dash, the lower first (1-3), or one level (4).

pane.history_empty: No changes to this task since recording started on {date}.
edit.conflict_title: This task changed while you were editing
edit.conflict_body: Someone (a person or an AI agent) saved a newer version after you started, so yours was not saved. Your text is still in the box above. Compare it with the newer one below, copy what you need from both, then choose.
edit.waiting_on_hint: Saving also makes the task Waiting, as alm wait does.
edit.backlog_held: Backlog is not offered while {holder} holds this task. Once it is released (alm release), it can be sent back to backlog.
edit.backlog_finished: A done or dropped task does not go back to backlog. If more work is needed, reopen it with alm reopen.
edit.name_explain: Allomos asks your name once and keeps it on this computer. The task's history records your changes under your pseudonym ID, never your name.
who.title: Who is making this change?
who.label_task: Your name (kept on this computer; the history holds only your pseudonym)
who.label: Your name (kept on this computer; the history holds only your pseudonym)
who.line: You are {name} on this computer; the history records your pseudonym.
who.line_none: Your name for changes is not set yet.
problem.not_json: This file could not be read as JSON for Allomos: {detail}.
problem.field_unknown: This version of Allomos does not know this field: a newer version may have added it (update, then look again), or its name is mistyped. It is kept as it is.
problem.invalid_choice: {value} is not a valid value here: it must be a word in quotes.
problem.value_unknown: This version of Allomos does not know the value {value}: a newer version may have added it (update, then look again), or it is mistyped. It is kept as it is, and this version does not change it.
problem.state_unknown: {id} has the state {state}, which this version of Allomos does not know, so it does not change it. Update Allomos, or correct the state in its file.
problem.folder_unknown: {folder} is not one of this taskbag's project folders ({folders}).
problem.folder_name_invalid: {name} is not a valid folder name: use lowercase letters, digits and -, at most 40.
problem.folder_name_taken: Two project folders are named {name}; each needs its own name.
problem.folder_choice_missing: Say which project folder this task belongs to: --folder <name> (repeatable) or --no-folder. This taskbag's folders: {folders}.
problem.upgrade_first: This taskbag is in {found}; task folders need {current}. Install the newest Allomos, then run alm upgrade (older Allomos versions refuse an upgraded taskbag).
problem.label_in_use: The label {label} cannot be removed from the label table: these tasks still carry it: {tasks}. Remove it from them first.
problem.invalid_id: "{id}" is not a valid ID. Use 1–64 letters, digits, '-' or '_'.
problem.wrong_format: Expected "{expected}" but found "{found}". This version of Allomos reads only "{expected}".
problem.label_exists: "{label}" is already in this project's label table.
problem.invalid_language: "{value}" is not a language. Use a language code such as en, zh-CN or ja, or ui to follow the Allomos app's language.
problem.duplicate_area_id: Another area already uses the ID "{id}".
problem.duplicate_task_id: Another task already uses the ID "{id}".
problem.unknown_area: The area "{area}" does not exist. Add areas/{area}.json or use an existing area ID.
problem.label_not_in_table: "{label}" is not in this project's label table ({labels}).
problem.label_added_to_table: Added the label {label} to this project's label table (it was not in it yet). If that was a typo, remove it from {id} and from the table.
problem.label_built_in: {label} is a built-in label: it cannot be removed or renamed.
problem.label_not_by_human: {label} is not a human-check label: use locally verified by human or deployed and verified by human.
problem.human_check_label_missing: {id} has no human-check label yet. If a person checked it, mark it checked first; otherwise finish it without the human check.
problem.no_signing_key: This computer has no signing key: Allomos keeps it in the system's key store, and has none it can use here yet (it has the macOS Keychain and the Windows Credential Manager). Nothing was written. Changes made here are written unsigned, and alm audit lists them.
problem.taskbag_to_upgrade: This taskbag is in {found}; this Allomos reads it but writes only {current}, whose labels have a new shape. Nothing was changed. Update the taskbag first (Update the taskbag…, or alm upgrade); older Allomos versions refuse an upgraded taskbag.
problem.waiting_on_missing: A waiting task must say what it is waiting on.
problem.without_human_check_missing: Say why the task is finished without the human check.
problem.branch_invalid: "{name}" is not a branch name. Give the branch's real name, as your version control tool shows it (in Git: `git branch --show-current`, for example main).
problem.trace_invalid: "{reference}" is neither a requirement ID nor a decision number. Give a requirement as REQUIREMENTS.md numbers it (for example R77) or a decision by its number (for example 0021).
problem.classify_invalid: "{value}" is not a {field} Allomos knows. Give one of: {allowed}.
problem.branch_missing: Allomos was not told which branch the agent is on, so task {id}'s branches were not recorded. Pass --branch <name>, as your version control tool shows it (in Git: `git branch --show-current`).
problem.base_differs: {held} starts from and merges into {held_base}, but the new task got the base {base}.
problem.iteration_active_already: {active} is the active iteration; only one iteration is active at a time. Close it first (or set it back to planned), then make {id} active.
problem.second_active_iteration: {id} is marked active, but {active} already is; only one iteration is active at a time. Set one of them to planned or closed.
problem.invalid_iteration_state: “{value}” is not an iteration state. Use planned, active or closed.
problem.duplicate_iteration_id: Another iteration already uses the ID "{id}".
problem.unknown_iteration: The iteration "{iteration}" does not exist. Add it with `alm add iteration`, or use an existing iteration ID.
problem.invalid_date: "{value}" is not a date. Write it as YYYY-MM-DD, for example 2026-10-08.
problem.task_file_missing: This task folder has no task.json.
problem.folder_not_empty: {path} is not empty, so no taskbag was created there.
problem.create_failed: Could not create the taskbag in {path}: {detail}.
problem.taskbag_not_found: No taskbag was found at or above {path}. Run `alm init` first, or pass --taskbag <path>.
problem.taskbag_unreadable: The taskbag at {path} could not be read: {detail}
problem.taskbag_busy: Another Allomos writer is changing the taskbag at {path}. Try again in a moment.
problem.holder_missing: Say who you are with --as <name> or the ALLOMOS_HOLDER environment variable.
problem.not_held: Task {id} is {state} and held by no working session, so it gets no heartbeat. Only the session holding an in-progress task beats (`alm claim` it first).
problem.heartbeat_minutes_invalid: "{value}" is not a length of whole minutes for {field}. Write it like 10m, 30m, 1h or 45 (minutes); at least 1 minute.
problem.busy_invalid: "{value}" is not a length of time. Write it like 45m, 2h or 1h30m (0m ends a busy window).
problem.request_reused: The one-time number {id} was already used for a different change, so nothing was done. Use a new number for a new change.
problem.task_changed: Task {id} changed after you read it, so your change was not saved. Read it again (its version is now {version}), then save.
problem.task_closed: Task {id} is {state}, so it cannot be changed this way.
problem.took_over_lost: Took task {id} over from {previous}: it was lost, with no sign of work from {previous} since {since}.
problem.taken_over: Task {id} was taken over by {by} at {at}: you no longer hold it. Stop work on it: no more commits or pushes to its working branch, and do not claim it back. Leave your worktree as it is, tell the person the task was taken over and by whom, and go on with another ready task (`alm next`) or end.
problem.merge_conflict: This file has conflict markers from your version control tool: two changes to it met when you got the latest changes. alm cannot read it until the conflict is resolved.
problem.claim_lost: Task {id} was claimed by two sessions at once, and the claim of {holder} (last heartbeat {at}) was shared first: the task is {holder}'s, not yours. Do not work on it. Drop your own claim, the change your version control tool could not share (in Git, during `git pull --rebase`: `git rebase --skip`; after a plain `git pull`: `git merge --abort`, then `git pull --rebase` and `git rebase --skip`), then take another ready task (`alm next`).
problem.claim_race: Task {id} was claimed by two sessions at once: {first} (last heartbeat {first_at}) and {second} (last heartbeat {second_at}). The claim that was shared first, the one that came in with the latest changes, holds the task; the session whose push was refused drops its own claim (`git rebase --skip` during `git pull --rebase`) and takes another ready task.
problem.link_refused: Allomos opens only web links and text files (.md, .txt) inside this project, so it did not open "{link}".
problem.open_failed: Could not open {path} in the file manager: {detail}.
problem.no_session: Task {id} records no session to open.
problem.update_failed: Allomos could not install the update: {detail}. You still have the version you had.
problem.agent_not_found: The AI agent {agent} was not found on this computer. Look for agents again.
problem.confirm_declined: The person chose Cancel in Allomos, so nothing should change.
problem.confirm_timeout: No answer came from the Allomos app within {seconds} seconds, so nothing should change. Open the project folder in the app and ask again.
problem.request_not_found: The question {id} is no longer waiting for an answer.
problem.startup_not_a_folder: Allomos was started with {path}, which is not a folder, so nothing was opened.
problem.cannot_make_ready: Task {id} is {state}; only a backlog, waiting or blocked task that no one holds can be made ready.
problem.cannot_set_state: Task {id} cannot be set to {state} here: a task becomes in progress only when an agent claims it (`alm claim`).
problem.cannot_back_to_backlog: Task {id} is {state}; only a ready, waiting or blocked task that no one holds can go back to backlog. A held task is released first (alm release); a finished one is reopened (alm reopen).
connect.title: Connect with the agents
connect.body: Choose one of your AI agents to connect the taskbag to your project folder. Allomos opens the agent in your project folder with a request already typed in. Nothing is sent until you send it yourself in the agent, except Antigravity, which takes the request and sends it at once. The request asks the agent to add Allomos's instructions to AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (creating either file if it is missing), so every new session knows how to work with the taskbag.
connect.asked: Opened {agent}. Read the request there and send it.
connect.asked_sent: Opened {agent} in a terminal, and the request was sent to it at once. Read its reply there.
connect.asked_paste: Opened {agent} in a terminal. Paste the request with {keys}, read it, and press Enter to send it.
notice.restart_agents: New in the project folder: {files}. AI agents read these files only when a session starts, so sessions that were already open in this project don't know about Allomos yet. Start a new session to use it.
welcome.hint: Select a folder where you want to keep your tasks.
recent.title: Open recent
wizard.title: Set up the taskbag
done.title: Setup done
done.body: This project is set up: your AI agents know about Allomos, its instructions are up to date, and no card files are left outside the taskbag.
wizard.what_body: A taskbag holds your project's tasks: what is planned, who is working on what, how far each task has got, and the notes one person or AI agent leaves for the next. It is a folder of plain text files named {dir}, so you can keep it in your version control tool (for example Git) with your project. You see it here in Allomos; AI agents use it through the alm command.
wizard.choose_hint: Choose the folder where the taskbag should go. Usually this is your project's own folder: {dir} is then created inside it.
wizard.found_title: This folder already has a taskbag
wizard.found_body: Allomos will use the taskbag in {path}. To use another one, choose Previous and pick a different folder.
wizard.missing_title: No taskbag in this folder yet
wizard.missing_body: Allomos will create {dir} in {folder}, with an empty taskbag inside. Nothing else in the folder changes.
wizard.task_language_hint: AI agents write tasks in this language. You can change it later in Settings → Tasks.
wizard.git_agent: In step 4, the AI agent you connect asks you whether to keep this folder under version control (for Git: `git init`, if it is not yet), then saves the taskbag there; nothing is shared.
wizard.source_title: Connect the folders that hold your project
wizard.source_body: A project folder holds code, documents and the instruction files AI agents read (AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md). One taskbag can serve several, for example a code, a website and a mobile repository. Start with the folder that holds the taskbag, and add others now or later in Settings.
wizard.folders_hint: In step 4, the agent you connect sets up AGENTS.md in each of these folders.
wizard.created_body: Allomos created a new, empty taskbag in {path} and will use it.
welcome.lede: Your AI agent or account hits its usage limit, and you have to switch. A teammate gets stuck on a hard problem and hands the task to you. Whoever takes over picks up exactly where it stopped. The whole project stays on the record — every task, its status and its handoff notes, in one place, the project's taskbag (plain files in your own repository), instead of scattered across chats.
fig.title: A task shifts from Claude Code (account 1) to Codex (account 2) when the quota is used up, then to a teammate at hand-off; all three read and write the same taskbag in the repository.
problem.taskbag_newer: This taskbag was written by a newer Allomos (format {found}), while the current app reads {supported}. Update Allomos now to work with it.
problem.instructions_outdated: Allomos's instructions in {files} are out of date (this Allomos writes version {current}).
update.notice_section: Allomos's instructions in {files} are out of date. An AI agent can renew them.
update.title: Update the instructions
update.body: Choose one of your AI agents. Allomos opens it in your project folder with a request already typed in, asking it to renew Allomos's instructions in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md for this Allomos. Nothing is sent until you send it yourself. Allomos does not change these files itself.
update.no_agent: No AI agent was found on this computer. Allomos does not change these files itself: choose Manual to paste the request into any AI agent.
update.asked: Opened {agent}. Read the request there and send it. The notice goes away once the agent has updated the project.
update.asked_sent: Opened {agent} in a terminal, and the request was sent to it at once. The notice goes away once the agent has updated the project.
update.asked_paste: Opened {agent} in a terminal. Paste the request with {keys}, read it, and press Enter to send it. The notice goes away once the agent has updated the project.
update.preparing: Allomos {latest} is available. Its installer is being prepared.
update.downloading: Allomos {latest} is available. Its installer is downloading: {percent}%.
update.check_failed: Couldn't reach GitHub to check for a newer Allomos. Try again later.
problem.invalid_percent: "{value}" is not a percentage. Use a whole number from 0 to 100.
problem.handoff_empty: Say where the work stopped and the one next step.
handoff_settings.body: When AI agents working this project must write their handoff into the task they hold (its handoff note) and release it, so the next session picks it up. The gates apply only while an agent holds a task. Agents are told these rules by alm next and alm handoff-rules.
handoff_settings.quota: Quota gate: with this much of the 5-hour quota left, start nothing new, write the handoff, release the task and stop
handoff_settings.context: Context gate: at this much of the context used, write the handoff, release the task and hand over to a new session
handoff_settings.overrides: Own gates for an agent or account
handoff_settings.overrides_body: A name such as codex or claude/work. Its gates win over the project's; an empty one follows the project.
heartbeat_settings.body: A session holding a task shows it is still at work with a heartbeat (alm beat). After the lost limit with no heartbeat and no busy window running, the task is marked Lost in the task list and alm next offers it to other sessions to take over. Agents learn these numbers from alm heartbeat-settings.
heartbeat_settings.interval: Heartbeat interval: a session holding a task beats at least this often
heartbeat_settings.lost_after: Lost after: a held task with no heartbeat for longer is lost
heartbeat_settings.too_short: The lost limit is not longer than the interval, so a task can be marked Lost between two regular heartbeats.
box.needs_newer_app: The tasks show once Allomos is updated.
create.name_explain: Allomos asks your name once and keeps it on this computer. The history records what you add under your pseudonym ID, never your name.
create.title: Title
create.base_hint: Open tasks start from different branches: pick the one this task starts from and merges back into.
create.base_same: Base branch: {base}, like every open task.
create.task_hint: The task starts in Backlog, as with alm add task.
create.name: Name
group_edit.delete_area_confirm: Delete area {id}? This works only when no task is in it, counting done and dropped ones.
group_edit.delete_iteration_confirm: Delete iteration {id}? This works only when no task is planned in it, counting done and dropped ones.
problem.area_not_empty: The area "{id}" cannot be deleted: {count} task(s) are in it, counting done and dropped ones. An area can be deleted only when no task is in it.
problem.iteration_not_empty: The iteration "{id}" cannot be deleted: {count} task(s) are planned in it, counting done and dropped ones. Plan them in another iteration, or take them out of it, first.
edit.blocked_by_legend: The tasks that must finish first
edit.folders_legend: The project folders this task belongs to
edit.no_folders: No project folder is bound to this taskbag yet.
edit.blocked_by_hint: Saving also makes the task Blocked, as alm block does.
edit.new_iteration_hint: Saving adds this iteration and plans the task in it, as alm add iteration and alm plan do.
edit.new_iteration_hint_id: Saving adds iteration {id} and plans the task in it, as alm add iteration and alm plan do.
filter.label: Show
problem.blocked_by_missing: A blocked task must name the task(s) that must finish first.
problem.blocker_unknown: There is no task "{id}" in this taskbag, so it cannot block another task.
problem.blocked_by_self: Task {id} cannot be blocked by itself.
problem.not_blocked: Task {id} is {state}, not blocked, so there is nothing to unblock.
problem.blocker_dropped: {blocker}, which blocks {id}, is dropped: a dropped blocker counts as finished, so it holds {id} back no longer.
pane.no_steps: No human check steps were written. Ask the agent to add them.
pane.checked_hint: You tried it by hand and it works: it gets the label “{label}” and leaves To check. The note and the steps stay in its history. For the other “by human” label, change its labels instead.
problem.human_check_steps_missing: No human check steps for {id}: a person must be able to pick it up and test it. Write them in Markdown (the test folder, what to open, what to click, what they should see) and add them with --steps.
problem.human_check_steps_empty: The human check steps are empty. Write what a person opens, clicks and should see.
problem.not_done: Task {id} is {state}, not done: only a finished task is human-checked.
task.ai_decided_title: An AI agent decided {count} thing(s) here on its own. Open the task to review them.
pane.reviewed_hint: You have read these decisions: they leave To review and the badge goes away; the history keeps them. To overturn one, change the task as usual.
problem.ai_decision_missing: Say what was decided and why, in one line.
problem.nothing_to_review: Task {id} has no AI decisions waiting for review.
pane.reopen_hint: More work on this task's outcome: it becomes ready again, held by nobody, with your reason in its history. Its label and human-check record are cleared (the history keeps them); the description and handoff note stay.
problem.link_kind_unknown: "{kind}" is not a kind of link: give commit, branch, merge, pr, ci or release.
problem.link_ref_invalid: "{reference}" cannot be a {kind} link: a commit or merge is given by its hash.
problem.link_url_invalid: "{url}" is not a web address: give one that starts with https://.
problem.exception_kind_unknown: "{kind}" is not a kind of exception. Give one of: check not run, without the human check, other.
problem.exception_incomplete: An exception needs why the control was skipped: give {missing}.
pane.exception_not_accepted: nobody named as accepting the risk
problem.retention_invalid: "{value}" is not a retention period: use forever, or a number of years from 1 to 100 (for example 7).
problem.legal_hold_on: A legal hold is on in this project: nothing in the history may be removed or redacted. It is turned off in Settings → this taskbag → Audit, with a reason.
problem.witness_service_invalid: "{value}" is not a time-stamp service: choose one from the list, or enter an address starting with https:// (or http://).
problem.witness_not_confirmed: Turning the outside witness on sends each checkpoint's fingerprint (never the content) to the chosen service, so it needs your confirmation.
problem.witness_off: The outside witness is off: turn it on first to choose its services.
problem.witness_when_invalid: “{value}” is not how often to make checkpoints: choose every day, at each approval and human check, or only when you ask.
problem.redact_field_missing: Name the field to remove (for example the description or the handoff note).
problem.redact_reason_missing: Say why the details are removed; the reason is recorded, the removed values are not.
problem.redact_field_unknown: Task {id}'s history has no change of the field "{field}".
problem.redact_event_unknown: {file} is not an event of task {id}.
audit.retention_help: Removing personal details changes the files from now on. Older versions stay in Git history unless the history is rewritten, which the audit check will then report.
audit.retention_law: China's Cybersecurity Law (Art. 23) asks for network logs to be kept at least six months.
audit.legal_hold_help: While it is on, nothing in the history can be removed or redacted. Turning it on or off asks why.
audit.always_help: Allomos always records who made each change, approvals, human checks, links to code, outside effects and reasons. These cannot be turned off.
audit.standards_map: See which settings each standard needs
audit.always_who: Who ran each change (agent, model, session) and for whom
audit.always_approvals: Approvals: who approved what, when, how, and when it expires
audit.always_checks: Human checks: who checked, against which steps, and the result
audit.always_links: Links to commits, branches, pull requests, CI runs and releases
audit.always_effects: Outside effects: target, action, how to undo it, approval and result
audit.always_reasons: Reasons for state and plan changes
audit.always_exceptions: Exceptions: checks not run, and who accepted the risk
audit.always_ai: AI details: model, effort, permission mode, rules version and alm version
audit.always_signed: Signed events and checkpoints, so a removed or changed event can be found (allomos/8)
audit.witness_help: A time-stamp service countersigns the taskbag's fingerprint, so the history can be shown to have existed in this form at that time. Some services charge per time-stamp.
audit.witness_switch: Have checkpoints countersigned by a time-stamp service
audit.witness_presets_note: FreeTSA is free and allows commercial use, with no promise of service. DigiCert, Sectigo and GlobalSign run their servers for code signing and do not say whether they may be used this way. For audits that need a qualified time stamp, enter your provider's address.
audit.witness_when_approvals: At each approval and human check
audit.witness_when_daily_note: Once a day a checkpoint is made and its fingerprint sent: by the app while it is open, or by the next alm command that changes the taskbag. Offline, it waits and is sent later.
audit.witness_when_approvals_note: A checkpoint is made and its fingerprint sent after each approval and each human check, in the app or with alm. Offline, it waits and is sent later.
audit.witness_when_asked_note: Checkpoints are made only with Make a checkpoint now, alm checkpoint, and when upgrading.
audit.witness_confirm: Only a fingerprint of the taskbag is sent to the service you choose, never its content. It is sent with every checkpoint from now on.
audit.witness_waiting: Fingerprints waiting to be sent: {count} (they go with the next checkpoint).
audit.witness_still_waiting: Not sent yet: {count}. They are kept and sent with the next checkpoint; the receipt will carry that later time. ({why})
audit.checkpoint_no_key: This computer has no key store for Allomos, so it cannot sign a checkpoint.
audit.redact_help: Removes every past value of the chosen fields from one task's history, wherever it differs from the current value. The history keeps an event saying which fields were removed, who approved it and why, never the old values. The current value stays: change it first.
audit.redact_hold: A legal hold is on: nothing can be removed until it is turned off.
audit.redact_approved_by_help: A pseudonym ID or a role, never an email address: the history keeps it for good.
audit.redact_nothing: Nothing removed: every past value of these fields is the current one or was removed before.
audit.change_types_help: Emergency changes may go ahead first; their approval is recorded afterwards, by the deadline shown.
audit.type_normal: Normal: approved before it is made
audit.type_emergency: Emergency: made first, approved afterwards by a deadline
audit.change_types_fixed: These types and risk levels are fixed; a project cannot rename them.
this_computer.title: This computer
this_computer.key_help: This computer signs every change it writes. The private key stays in this computer's key store.
this_computer.no_key_yet: No key yet: this computer makes one with its first change to an allomos/8 taskbag.
this_computer.no_store: This computer has no key store for Allomos: its changes are written unsigned, and the audit lists them as such.
this_computer.seen_help: If a taskbag's history is rewritten, Allomos tells you here and in the task list.
this_computer.seen_none: None yet: the audit check remembers the last checkpoint it saw of each taskbag.
this_computer.seen_gone: no longer in its history: it was rewritten or the checkpoint removed
this_computer.seen_unknown: not among the recent folders, so not checked
problem.signing_key_not_saved: The new signing key could not be saved in this computer's key store, so the key was not replaced. Nothing was written to any taskbag; the old key is still this computer's.
this_computer.replaced_failed: These taskbags could not be written, so the old key is not retired there yet: {taskbags}
this_computer.replaced: Key replaced. The old key {old} is retired in {count} taskbags.
this_computer.replace_help: Allomos makes a new signing key for this computer. In every recent folder's taskbag that has the old key, the old public key stays in keys/, marked retired, so the changes it signed can still be checked, and the new key is added; each is a signed change. Other taskbags get the new key with this computer's next change there. Replace it when you think the old key was copied, or on your company's schedule.
this_computer.store_folder: Kept in this trial run's settings folder, not in the system's key store.
this_computer.store_credential_manager: Kept in the Windows Credential Manager (generic credential io.allomos.signing/this-computer).
this_computer.store_keychain: Kept in the macOS login Keychain (item "Allomos signing key").
problem.effect_incomplete: An outside effect needs where it acts, what it does and how it is undone: give {missing}.
pane.reopen_placeholder: Why it is reopened, for example what failed in the check
problem.cannot_reopen: Task {id} is {state}: only a done or dropped task can be reopened. It is still open, so carry on with it as it is.
problem.cannot_release: Task {id} is {state}: a finished task is held by no working session, so there is nothing to release. To work on it again, reopen it: `alm reopen {id} --note "<why>"`.
problem.reopen_note_missing: Say why the task is reopened.
search.label: Search tasks and handoffs
search.nothing: Nothing found for “{query}”: no task or handoff holds these words.
filter.grid_hint: A task is listed when it matches any tick in its state’s row.
filter.human_hint: Yes: a person checked it (it carries a “by human” label). No: it carries neither.
filter.row_hint: Sums up this row: all, some or none ticked. Click to tick or untick the whole row.
filter.empty_all: Nothing is ticked, so the list is empty.
filter.presets_hint: A preset only sets the ticks in Custom; change any of them there and it is no longer the preset.
filter.preset_ticks.needs_you: Done but not checked by a human, every Waiting task, and any task with AI decisions to review
filter.close: Close: the filter stays as it is
search.banner_filtered: {who} found for “{query}” with the “{filter}” filter on.
filter.banner.both: Filter and search together: only tasks that {verb} and hold “{query}” are listed, {where}.
filter.banner.none_both: None of the tasks found for “{query}” {verb}.
filter.matches_hidden.more_one: {count} more match is hidden by the filter.
filter.matches_hidden.more_other: {count} more matches are hidden by the filter.
filter.matches_hidden.all_one: The {count} match is hidden by the filter.
filter.matches_hidden.all_other: All {count} matches are hidden by the filter.
filter.left.area_one: The {count} area with none is left out.
filter.left.area_other: The {count} areas with none are left out.
filter.all_left.area_one: The only area is left out.
filter.left.iteration_one: The {count} iteration with none is left out.
filter.left.iteration_other: The {count} iterations with none are left out.
filter.all_left.iteration_one: The only iteration is left out.
problem.taskbag_to_move_in: This taskbag was written by an older Allomos (format {found}); this Allomos writes {current} and does not read older taskbags. An AI agent moves its tasks into a new taskbag: choose Update the taskbag… above.
problem.nothing_to_move_in: There is nothing to move in: the taskbag at {path} is not from an older Allomos.
move.notice_old: This taskbag was written by an older Allomos (format {found}), so its tasks are not shown. An AI agent can move them into a new taskbag. Allomos keeps the old folder beside it, renamed, until the agent's plan, which you confirm, removes it.
move.notice_waiting: The tasks of the older taskbag in {old} are not moved in yet. An AI agent can move them.
move.wizard_old: This taskbag was written by an older Allomos (format {found}). Update the taskbag… renames it aside, creates a new taskbag in its place, and then asks an AI agent to move the tasks across. Nothing in the old folder is changed.
move.found: Allomos found a taskbag written by an older Allomos (format {found}), now kept in {old}. Its tasks are not shown until an AI agent moves them into the new taskbag, with their card files.
move.title: Update the taskbag
move.body: Choose one of your AI agents. Allomos opens it in your project folder with a request already typed in, asking it to move the older taskbag's tasks, handoff notes and project notes into the new one (its history stays in your version control tool's history). The agent first shows you its plan in Allomos: nothing changes until you choose Go ahead, and the old folder is removed only as part of that plan. Nothing is sent until you send it yourself.
move.asked: Opened {agent}. Read the request there and send it. The notice goes away once the agent has moved the tasks in.
move.asked_sent: Opened {agent} in a terminal, and the request was sent to it at once. The notice goes away once the agent has moved the tasks in.
move.asked_paste: Opened {agent} in a terminal. Paste the request with {keys}, read it, and press Enter to send it. The notice goes away once the agent has moved the tasks in.
box.move_in: The tasks show once an AI agent has moved them into a new taskbag.
refresh.opened: Loaded at {time}, when the taskbag was opened
refresh.auto: Refreshed automatically at {time} · the taskbag files changed
refresh.manual_none: Refreshed by you at {time} · nothing changed
refresh.manual_settings: Refreshed by you at {time} · no task changed; areas, iterations or the project did
refresh.manual_tasks_one: Refreshed by you at {time} · {count} task changed ({ids})
refresh.manual_tasks_other: Refreshed by you at {time} · {count} tasks changed ({ids})
build.title: Build a new app
build.intro: Describe the app you want. Allomos sets up a taskbag in an empty folder and types one request into your AI agent; you read it and press Enter. The agent then plans the app into areas, iterations and tasks and builds it release by release. You see every step here.
build.folder_title: An empty folder for the app
build.folder_hint: Choose an empty folder (or make a new one): the agent builds the app there.
build.folder_pick: Choose an empty folder for the new app
build.folder_not_empty: {path} is not empty. Choose an empty folder, or open this one with Start instead.
build.taskbag_at: The taskbag (the app's tasks, progress and handoff notes) is made in {path}.
build.taskbag_pick: Choose a folder for the new app's taskbag
build.taskbag_has_one: {path} already holds a taskbag. This is not allowed: each taskbag belongs to one project folder. The change was discarded.
build.description_placeholder: In your own words: what it does, who uses it, where it runs…
build.mode_quiet_how: it goes on without you, decides routine things itself and parks questions for later
build.mode_normal_how: it stops and asks whenever it needs you
build.mode_more: What each mode means, and what you do afterwards
build.auto_mode: To run unattended, the agent needs its own auto mode (for example Claude Code's auto mode, or Codex's full access). Allomos never changes an agent's permissions; without it, the agent stops to ask before each step.
build.browser_checks: Checks in the browser can still ask you for clicks during the run: when the app is opened on a local network address (such as 192.168.x.x), the browser asks you to approve each script it runs there. The agent checks with tests and the command line first, and says in a task's steps when a check needs the browser.
build.discuss_intro: Shape the app with your agent before it builds anything.
build.discuss_wait: Once you send the request, the agent turns your description into the goal task and waits for you.
build.discuss_refine: Refine the goal with the agent in that conversation.
build.discuss_go: When it's right, tell the agent to go ahead, in any words. It plans and builds the app in the mode you chose.
build.asked_discuss: The agent writes the goal task first. Talk the goal over with it, then tell it to start when you are ready.
build.asked: Opened {agent} with the request typed in. Read it and press Enter to send it. The areas, iterations and tasks the agent makes appear here as it works.
build.asked_sent: Opened {agent} in a terminal, and the request was sent to it at once. The areas, iterations and tasks the agent makes appear here as it works.
build.asked_paste: Opened {agent} in a terminal. Paste the request with {keys}, read it, and press Enter to send it. The areas, iterations and tasks the agent makes appear here as it works.
build.manual_intro: Open your AI agent in {path}, paste this request there and press Enter. The areas, iterations and tasks it makes appear here as it works.
build.manual_done: Send the copied request in your AI agent. The areas, iterations and tasks it makes appear here as it works.
build.not_started: The taskbag is ready, but no agent was asked to build the app. To try again, choose Build a new app… on the start page with another empty folder.
lan.title: Devices on your network
lan.switch: Allow devices on your network to view
lan.body: While this is on, a phone or another computer on the same Wi-Fi or network can open Allomos in its browser. They can only look, never change anything. While it is off, nothing on the network can reach Allomos. Allomos remembers your choice.
lan.open: On the other device, scan the code or open
lan.no_network: Allomos is listening on port {port}, but this computer has no network address right now. Connect to a Wi-Fi or network, then open this window again.
lan.port_moved: Port {default} was taken, so Allomos uses port {port}.
lan.warning: The first time a device opens the address, its browser warns that the connection is not private. That is expected: the connection is encrypted with a certificate this computer made for itself, which no public authority has signed. Choose to continue (often under Advanced or Show details). It happens once per device.
lan.fingerprint: This computer's certificate fingerprint (SHA-256), to compare with what the browser shows:
lan.firewall: The first time this is on, macOS or Windows may ask whether Allomos may accept incoming network connections. Allow it, or other devices cannot connect.
lan.pairing_how: To pair a device, open the address above on it and enter a name there. Its request appears here for you to approve; then this window shows a code to type on the device.
lan.asks: “{name}” asks to connect. Approve it only if it is your device.
lan.code_rules: It works once and runs out in {time}. {tries} wrong tries left before it is replaced by a new code.
companion.no_app: Can't reach Allomos. Open the Allomos desktop app on your computer and turn on Devices on Your Network: this page connects again by itself.
companion.connected: Connected to the Allomos desktop app ({version}).
companion.wrong_code: That code is not right. {tries} tries left.
companion.new_code: Too many wrong tries: the desktop app now shows a new code. Type the new one.
companion.removed: This device was removed on the computer. Pair it again to use it.
companion.pair_intro: Pair this device once with the Allomos desktop app. Give it a name the person at the computer will recognise.
companion.name_hint: The name is recorded in the taskbag's history, which may be shared through Git: do not use an email address or other personal details.
companion.waiting: Waiting for approval on the computer: open Allomos there, File → Devices on Your Network…, and approve this device.
companion.type_code: Approved. Type the 9-digit code the desktop app shows.
companion.refused: The request was refused on the computer.
companion.expired: The request or its code ran out. Ask again.
companion.paired: Paired as “{device}”. This browser remembers it.
companion.open_taskbags: Taskbags open in the desktop app:
companion.none_open: The desktop app has no taskbag open right now.
companion.warning: If your browser warned that the connection is not private: that is expected. The desktop app encrypts the connection with a certificate it made for itself.
cards.notice: {count} tasks keep their card files in the project folder. An AI agent can move each one into the taskbag, beside its task.
cards.title: Update the taskbag
cards.update: Updating the taskbag moves each card file into the taskbag, beside its task, and points the task's Card: link to it, so each task is kept in one place.
cards.found_none: Allomos found no task whose Card: link points outside the taskbag. An AI agent can still look for card files kept in the project folder.
cards.found: Allomos found {count} tasks whose card file is still in the project folder, outside the taskbag.
cards.body: An AI agent does it. Choose one: Allomos opens it in your project folder with the request already typed in. The agent also looks for card files that no link names, then shows you its whole plan in Allomos: nothing changes until you choose Go ahead. Nothing is sent until you send it yourself.
cards.translate_no: Nothing is translated: tasks, card files and project notes stay in the language they are written in.
translate.button_note: An AI agent rewrites every task, iteration name, card file and handoff note in the language you choose, and the task language becomes that language.
translate.title: Translate the taskbag
translate.what: The agent rewrites every task's title, description and handoff note, every iteration's name, the card files and the project notes in this language, replacing the old text. Commands, task and iteration IDs, file paths and code stay as they are.
translate.sets_language: The task language changes to {language} too, so new tasks are written in it.
translate.sets_language_any: The task language changes to the chosen language too, so new tasks are written in it.
translate.manual_intro: Copy this request into any AI agent working in the project folder.
translate.asked: Opened {agent}. Read the request there and send it. The agent shows its plan here before it changes anything.
translate.asked_sent: Opened {agent} in a terminal, and the request was sent to it at once. The agent shows its plan here before it changes anything.
translate.asked_paste: Opened {agent} in a terminal. Paste the request with {keys}, read it, and press Enter to send it. The agent shows its plan here before it changes anything.
language_menu.hint: Type a language's name, in itself or in English.
cards.translate_yes: The agent rewrites every task's title, description and handoff note, every iteration's name, the card files and the project notes in this language, replacing the old text. Commands, task and iteration IDs, file paths and code stay as they are.
cards.manual_intro: Copy this request into an AI agent working in your project folder, and send it.
cards.manual_intro_to: Copy this request, paste it into {agent} working in your project folder, and send it.
cards.only_agent: {agent} worked on this project last and is not registered yet under Agents set up in the project notes, so only {agent} is offered: it registers itself and updates the taskbag in one go.
cards.only_manual: {agent} worked on this project last and is not registered yet under Agents set up, but Allomos cannot open it with the request typed in. Copy the request and paste it into {agent}.
cards.asked: Opened {agent}. Read the request there and send it. The notice goes away once the agent has moved the cards in.
cards.asked_sent: Opened {agent} in a terminal, and the request was sent to it at once. The notice goes away once the agent has moved the cards in.
cards.asked_paste: Opened {agent} in a terminal. Paste the request with {keys}, read it, and press Enter to send it. The notice goes away once the agent has moved the cards in.
old_handoffs.notice: This taskbag still keeps {count} old handoff files in its handoffs folder. A handoff now lives in its task: an AI agent can move what is still useful into the tasks and remove the files.
old_handoffs.found: Allomos found {count} old handoff files in the taskbag's handoffs folder:
old_handoffs.body: An AI agent does it. Choose one: Allomos opens it in your project folder with the request already typed in. The agent reads each file, writes what is still useful into the tasks it names (their handoff note and evidence), and shows you its whole plan in Allomos: nothing changes until you choose Go ahead. Then it removes the files. Nothing is sent until you send it yourself.
old_handoffs.asked: Opened {agent}. Read the request there and send it. The notice goes away once the agent has moved the handoffs into their tasks.
old_handoffs.asked_sent: Opened {agent} in a terminal, and the request was sent to it at once. The notice goes away once the agent has moved the handoffs into their tasks.
old_handoffs.asked_paste: Opened {agent} in a terminal. Paste the request with {keys}, read it, and press Enter to send it. The notice goes away once the agent has moved the handoffs into their tasks.
empty.found: The taskbag has no tasks yet.
empty.body: An AI agent looks for the tasks this project already keeps (a task board, card files, a to-do list) and shows you its plan here in Allomos; it moves them into the taskbag only if you choose Go ahead. If it finds none, nothing changes.
empty.asked: Opened {agent}. Read the request there and send it. The agent shows you its plan here before anything changes.
empty.asked_sent: Opened {agent} in a terminal, and the request was sent to it at once. The agent shows you its plan here before anything changes.
empty.asked_paste: Opened {agent} in a terminal. Paste the request with {keys}, read it, and press Enter to send it. The agent shows you its plan here before anything changes.
pane.card_outside: Card file in the project folder
problem.card_path_invalid: "{path}" is not a card file's place: give its path inside the project folder, relative to that folder.
problem.card_exists: Task {id} already has a different card file, so it was not replaced.
problem.card_empty: The card file {path} is empty, so nothing was moved in.
problem.card_not_reported: No card file was reported for task {id}.
problem.claim_cards_outside: {count} task(s) keep their card files outside the taskbag ({tasks}), so no task can be claimed until they are moved in.
sort.label: Sort the tasks in each area or iteration
agents_section.body: Which AI agents are set up in this taskbag's project folders: their instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) point them to this taskbag.
agents_section.not_found: {name} is not found on this computer
upgrade.notice: This taskbag is in {found}; this Allomos writes {current}. An AI agent can upgrade it.
upgrade.found: This taskbag is in {found}. Updating upgrades it first: project folders and task folders need the newer format. The agent shows its plan in Allomos and changes nothing until you choose Go ahead.
upgrade.warning: After the upgrade, older Allomos versions (the app, alm, and every agent session using them) refuse this taskbag until the newest Allomos is installed.
upgrade.asked: Opened {agent}. Read the request there and send it. The notice goes away once the agent has upgraded the taskbag.
upgrade.asked_sent: Opened {agent} in a terminal, and the request was sent to it at once. The notice goes away once the agent has upgraded the taskbag.
upgrade.asked_paste: Opened {agent} in a terminal. Paste the request with {keys}, read it, and press Enter to send it. The notice goes away once the agent has upgraded the taskbag.
problem.companion_read_only: This can only be done on the computer itself, in the Allomos desktop app.
problem.companion_desktop_only: This can only be done on the computer itself, in the Allomos desktop app ({op}).
problem.companion_no_app: Can't reach the Allomos desktop app.
problem.companion_not_open: The desktop app no longer has this taskbag open.
proceed.button_title: Open an AI agent to work on this task
proceed.title: Work on it with an AI agent
proceed.title_ask: Ask an AI agent about this task
proceed.found: {id} {title} is {state}, and no session holds it.
proceed.found_blocked: {id} {title} is {state} by {by}, so it cannot start now.
proceed.found_waiting: {id} {title} is {state} on: {on}. It cannot start now.
proceed.edited: Edited: the agent gets your text.
proceed.backlog: This task is in Backlog. Choosing Open approves it: the agent makes it ready, then claims it.
proceed.does: An AI agent claims the task and works on it in a worktree of its own. Its progress shows here as it goes.
proceed.does_blocked: The AI agent looks at it first: it tells you why it is stopped and what could be done, then asks what you want it to do. It changes nothing until you answer.
proceed.does_waiting: The AI agent looks at it first: it tells you what it waits on and what could be done, then asks what you want it to do. It changes nothing until you answer.
proceed.how: An AI agent does it. Choose one: Allomos opens it in your project folder with the request already typed in. Nothing is sent until you send it yourself.
proceed.copied: ✓ Copied. Paste it into your AI agent and send it.
proceed.asked: Opened {agent}. Read the request there and send it. The row shows who holds {id} once the agent claims it.
proceed.asked_sent: Opened {agent} in a terminal, and the request was sent to it at once. The row shows who holds {id} once the agent claims it.
proceed.asked_paste: Opened {agent} in a terminal. Paste the request with {keys}, read it, and press Enter to send it. The row shows who holds {id} once the agent claims it.
proceed.asked_stopped: Opened {agent}. Read the request there and send it. The agent tells you why {id} is stopped and asks what to do.
proceed.asked_stopped_sent: Opened {agent} in a terminal, and the request was sent to it at once. The agent tells you why {id} is stopped and asks what to do.
proceed.asked_stopped_paste: Opened {agent} in a terminal. Paste the request with {keys}, read it, and press Enter to send it. The agent tells you why {id} is stopped and asks what to do.
proceed.edit_note: Allomos types this in for the agent you choose, or gives it to you to copy. Your changes are kept for this time only; next time the dialog starts from Allomos's request again.
monitor.button_none_tip: No task is ready now; once started, it checks at the frequency you set.
monitor.title: Monitor ready tasks
monitor.intro: Allomos works each ready task in a new agent session, one at a time: the next starts only when the last one is finished. With none ready, it waits and checks again.
monitor.current_note: The iteration under way. Build an app… splits the work into iterations.
monitor.no_iterations: No iterations yet. Add one on the Iterations tab to run only its tasks.
monitor.frequency: When no task is ready, check every
monitor.frequency_note: When tasks are ready, they are worked one after another, without waiting.
monitor.how_terminal: Allomos opens a terminal session for each task; unattended throughout
monitor.permissions_claude_cli: Each task gets a new Claude Code session, so turning on auto mode in one session (Shift+Tab) does not carry over to the next. Before you start, make auto mode Claude Code's default in its own settings; otherwise every session stops to ask for permission. Allomos never changes an agent's permissions.
monitor.permissions_codex_cli: Each task gets a new Codex session, with nobody there to approve its commands. With Allomos's rules for Codex (the option below), each session can pull, commit, push and merge, and run alm, without asking; every other command stays in Codex's sandbox. Without them, Codex cannot change its repository from its sandbox and stops.
monitor.codex_rules_add: Let Codex run Git and alm without asking (adds {path})
monitor.codex_rules_update: Let Codex run Git and alm without asking (updates {path})
monitor.codex_rules_keep: Let Codex run Git and alm without asking ({path}, version {version}; uncheck to remove it at Start)
monitor.codex_rules_replace: Replace it with Allomos's version {version} at Start
monitor.codex_rules_note: Unattended Codex sessions can then pull, commit, push and merge, and run alm; every other command stays in Codex's sandbox. Your own rules in default.rules are not touched. Nothing is written until you press Start.
monitor.codex_rules_changed_by: Allomos's Codex rules changed (version {from} → {to}): added {added}; removed {removed}. Unchecked, Codex keeps the old file this time.
monitor.codex_rules_edited: Someone changed {path}. Replacing it with Allomos's version {version} adds {added} and removes {removed}.
monitor.codex_rules_newer: {path} is version {version}, from a newer Allomos; this Allomos leaves it as it is.
monitor.permissions_antigravity_cli: Each task gets a new Antigravity session (agy), so a mode chosen in one session (Shift+Tab) does not carry over to the next. Before you start, set Antigravity's own default mode in its settings (~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json: "agentMode": "auto"); otherwise sessions may stop to ask before running commands. This setting applies to every agy session on this computer. Allomos never changes an agent's permissions.
monitor.later_app: Not available: there is no way to run the Claude app unattended from here. A session it opens cannot start new sessions on its own, and Allomos cannot set up its scheduled tasks.
monitor.later_manual: Not available: a request you paste yourself cannot run unattended.
monitor.mode_quiet_effect: Unattended: a session parks a real question (alm wait) and goes on; the monitor goes on to the next task.
monitor.mode_normal_effect: A session with a question stops to ask you; its task stays in progress, and the monitor starts the next only after you answer and it finishes.
monitor.backlog_note: New tasks stay in backlog until you approve them; once you make one ready, the next check takes it.
monitor.on_waiting: Monitoring · no task is ready; next check {time}
monitor.unblocked_ready: Unblocked automatically: {ids} (all their blockers have finished), now ready.
monitor.unblocked_in_progress: Unblocked automatically: {ids} (all their blockers have finished), now in progress.
monitor.stalled: {id}'s session has shown no sign of life for a long time
monitor.on_working_waiting: Monitoring · working on {id} (task {n}); no other task is ready, next check {time}
monitor.agents_note: Choose one or more. Each chosen agent works ready tasks in new sessions, one task per session (one session at a time unless you set more below). Each session claims its task first, so no two work the same one.
monitor.account_note: Pick the folder this account keeps its settings and login in. Allomos stores only the folder's path and the name you give it; it never reads the login. Its sessions run with that folder as the agent's settings folder.
monitor.agents_menu_note: An agent added gets tasks from the next check on. One taken off finishes the task it is working, then gets no more.
monitor.agents_last: At least one agent stays; to end the run, use Stop
monitor.sessions_note: Each session claims its own ready task first; when one finishes, the next ready task goes to the next session. A higher count starts the extra sessions at the next check; a lower one lets the sessions at work finish. No upper limit: more sessions keep this computer busier, use quota faster and cause more merge conflicts.
monitor.sessions_menu_note: A higher count starts sessions at the next check; a lower one lets the sessions at work finish.
monitor.levels_note: Each agent takes only the ready tasks in its levels, from 1 (very easy) to 5 (very hard); all levels unless you narrow them. A task with no level counts as 3.
monitor.levels_menu_note: A change applies from the next check on; a session at work is not interrupted.
monitor.no_task_in_levels: No ready task in the levels of {agents}, so no session starts for them.
monitor.last_run_need_tip: Show the tasks that need you (the Needs you preset)
monitor.start_failed: Monitoring stopped: {agent} could not be started for {id}. {detail}
monitor.close_prompt: Allomos: the task is done. This tab closes in 30 seconds; press any key to keep it.
monitor.lost: A monitor is running with its record missing (process {pid}) {id}
monitor.run_tip: Monitor {id}: alm monitor status shows it too
monitors.title: Monitors running on this computer
monitors.waiting: no task is ready; next check {time}
label.meaning.locally_by_agent: The agent built it and its checks passed on the computer where it worked.
label.meaning.deployed_by_agent: The agent deployed it (with the approver's approval) and checked it live.
label.meaning.locally_by_human: A person checked it by hand on their own computer (the human check).
label.meaning.deployed_by_human: A person checked it by hand in the deployed app (the human check).
label.meaning.ai_decisions: An agent decided things here that wait for review.
settings.labels_note: Every label is plain: a task has it or not, and a task can carry several. The five built-in labels are always here. A label given to a task that is not listed yet is added.
settings.own_labels_note: Renaming a label renames it on every task that carries it. A label tasks still carry cannot be removed.
settings.labels_duplicate: Two labels have the same name, or one has a built-in label's name.
task.not_human_checked_plain: Done, and no person has checked it yet: it carries no “by human” label.
edit.labels_none: No label in the table yet.
pane.approval_status.plan_changed: No longer applies: the plan changed
problem.approval_words_missing: Give the person's own words of approval, as they wrote them.
pane.approve_hint: Approve this task's plan: its description, as it is now. If the description changes later, the approval no longer applies.
pane.approve_no_plan: There is no plan to approve yet: the task has no description.
pane.approve_shown: You are approving this plan (the task's description, exactly as written):
pane.approve_plan_changed: The description changed while this was open. Close and open Approve… again to read the new plan.
pane.approve_state_hint: Approve does not change the task's state. Approve and make ready also makes it ready, as alm ready does.
pane.withdraw_hint: The approval then no longer applies; the history keeps it. Withdrawing does not stop the task: whoever holds it decides.
pane.approval_withdrawn_notice: Approval withdrawn ({at}) while this task is in progress. Nothing was stopped: whoever holds the task decides whether to stop.
problem.withdraw_reason_missing: Say why the approval is withdrawn.
audit.identity_help: The history only ever holds a pseudonym ID. Who is behind each one is kept on this computer (local project) or in the cloud (cloud project), never in the taskbag.
audit.reauthenticate: Sign in again to approve or check
audit.unknown_level: project.json says "{value}", which this Allomos does not know; it keeps the pseudonym.
audit.identities_where: Who is behind this computer's pseudonyms is kept in identities.json, in Allomos's settings folder.
problem.identity_level_unknown: "{value}" is not an identity level. Use pseudonym, account or sso.
problem.identity_needs_cloud: The identity level "{level}" needs a cloud project; this project is local-only, so it keeps the pseudonym.
problem.reauthenticate_needs_sign_in: Signing in again to approve or check needs the Allomos account or company sign-in (SSO) identity level; with a pseudonym there is nothing to sign in to.
problem.audit_reason_missing: Turning {setting} off or down needs a reason.
audit.separation_switch: The same person or agent may not both do and check (or do and approve) a task
audit.separation_help: Turn on when your company requires a second person. A project with one person cannot finish tasks while this is on.
problem.self_check: Separation of duties is on in this project: {who} worked on task {id}, so they may not also check it. Someone else checks it, or the switch is turned off with a reason.
problem.self_approve: Separation of duties is on in this project: {who} worked on task {id}, so they may not also approve it. Someone else approves it, or the switch is turned off with a reason.
problem.work_after_signing: Separation of duties is on in this project: {who} approved or checked task {id}, so they may not also work on it. Someone else works on it, or the switch is turned off with a reason.
problem.checker_unknown: Separation of duties is on in this project, and the check of task {id} names no checker, so Allomos cannot tell it is someone other than who did the work.
heartbeat.lost_title: No heartbeat for more than {minutes} minutes and no busy window running: another session can take it over (alm next lists the command).
takeover.button_title: Open a new AI agent session to take this lost task over and go on on its working branch
takeover.title: Take over a lost task
takeover.found: {id} {title} is held by {holder}, which {ago}: the task is lost.
takeover.branch: The new session goes on on its working branch, {branch}.
takeover.branch_unknown: No working branch is recorded; the new session goes on on the one the claim prints.
takeover.worktree: The former session's worktree may hold changes it never committed. The new session may look at them but changes nothing there.
takeover.does: A new AI agent session claims the task, which takes it over from the former holder, and goes on with the work in a worktree of its own.
takeover.asked: Opened {agent}. Read the request there and send it. The row shows the new holder of {id} once the agent claims it.
takeover.asked_sent: Opened {agent} in a terminal, and the request was sent to it at once. The row shows the new holder of {id} once the agent claims it.
takeover.asked_paste: Opened {agent} in a terminal. Paste the request with {keys}, read it, and press Enter to send it. The row shows the new holder of {id} once the agent claims it.
